messages:
sarah: Starting a config-only deploy now. Changes: routing policy nudged to prefer 'cheap-pool' for non-SLA, batching window 32ms -> 20ms, per-request token cap 2048 -> 1536. Canary 1% for 15m. Tagging @oncall-elaine. Change window 10:30-11:30 PT.

deploy-bot: STARTED canary config-release config-v2026-03-42 target=1% duration=15m
commands:
```
./deploy apply --release config-v2026-03-42 --canary 1%
```

raj: Quick Q: are we pinning model variants for the fallback path? don't want unexpected model swaps mid-rollout.

sarah: Yes pinned to model v3-q4 for this rollout. No model binaries changed — config-only. Release note will spell that out. Observability targets: watch token-level latency, p95, error-rate, KV cache hit.

anya: I'll watch dashboards. Alert triggers: error-rate > 0.5% OR p95 increase > 20% over baseline. Also watching KV cache hit drop > 10%. :eyes: 

mike: Rollback plan if triggered: immediate config flip to previous config and scale back cheap-pool routing. Rollback command:
```
./deploy rollback --release config-v2026-03-41 --force
```
Keep me in the loop and we'll pause traffic ramp.

deploy-bot: CANARY PASSED (15m). Promotion scheduled: 1% -> 25% for 10m. advancing...

oncall-elaine: Observability check: p95 +14% vs baseline, error-rate 0.12% -> holding. KV cache hit steady. No hit to SLA customers. OK to proceed to 25%.

raj: One more guard: let's cap cheap-pool qps to 60% during ramp to avoid sudden saturation. Recommend adding a soft throttle policy.

sarah: Added soft throttle guard to the config and re-deployed canary slice. Starting 25% -> 100% ramp over next 30m with staggered steps. Posting runbook updates to #eng-ops and adding note to release docs. Thanks all :tada:
